entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Baha' al-Din Naqshband (c. 1317-1389) was a Central Asian Sufi mystic and the founder of the Naqshbandi Sufi order, one of the largest and most influential Sufi Sunni orders in Islamic history. Born in present-day Uzbekistan, Naqshband traveled extensively throughout the Middle East, North Africa, and Central Asia, establishing a network of spiritual centers and attracting followers from diverse backgrounds. His teachings emphasized the importance of spiritual purification, inner transformation, and the attainment of spiritual realization through the cultivation of devotion, humility, and self-discipline. Through his teachings, Naqshband influenced the spiritual landscape of the Islamic world, shaping the development of Sufi thought and practice in the Ottoman Empire, India, and other regions. His legacy can be seen in the Naqshbandi order's continued presence in modern-day Pakistan, India, and Central Asia, as well as its impact on Sufi mysticism and Islamic spirituality more broadly.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Baha' al-Din Naqshband's teachings and legacy had a profound impact on the spiritual landscape of the Islamic world, shaping Sufi thought and practice in various regions and influencing the development of mysticism in the Indian subcontinent, North Africa, and other parts of the Islamic world.
